PREFACE 


In 
the 
following

I 
have 
confined 
myself 
in 
the 
main 
to

problems

philosophy

For

theory 
of 
knowledge

than 
metaphysics

the 
present

and 
some

much 
discussed

philosophersare 
treatedverybriefly, 
ifat 
all. 


I

unpublished

G.

Moore

M. 
Keynes: 
from 
the

as 
regards

and

I

and

ProfessorGilbertMurray.

Good

of 
logic. 
Does 
not 
this 
give 
a 
strong 
presumption, 
that 
those 
axioms 
which 
are 
retained, 
are 
retained 
because 
they 
are 
logically 
indispensable? 
If 
this 
be 
so, 
the 
axioms 
common 
to 
Euclid 
and 
Metageometry 
will 
be 
à 
priori, 
while 
those 
peculiar 
to 
Euclid 
will 
be 
empirical. 
After 
a 
criticism 
of 
some 
differing 
theories 
of 
Geometry, 
I 
shall 
proceed, 
in 
Chapters 
III. 
and 
IV., 
to 
the 
proof 
and 
consequences 
of 
this 
thesis, 
which 
will 
form 
the 
remainder 
of 
thepresentwork.

51. 
We

may

of 
the 
subject.

the

doctrine 
of 
space.

has

importance 
in

theoryofknowledge.

a 
criticism 
of 
representative 
modern 
theories

is

to

Measurement,

Using

Now 
a 
number, 
to 
begin 
with, 
is 
a

of

units, 
all

these

In

In

intensive; 
in 
the

extensive. 
A

therefore,

not 
numerable—a

consist 
of 
wholly 
unsynthesized 
particulars. 
A

similar 
parts. 
But

continuous

must

divisible. 
For

the 
points 
at

and 
so 
destroy

division

mutual 
externality. 
For

have 
seen,

which

Free 
Mobility 
and

impossible.

measurement

not

This

Sabotage

It

A

Another
